channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: Nvidia Chief, Jensen Huang, Is Seen as Target of Chinese Spy Plot
item.description: A Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing. President Trump was briefed and took no action.

item.title: NPR: US and Japan agree to establish a Japanese facility for joint missile production
item.description: The announcement Wednesday is the latest action by the allies, who have repeatedly expressed alarm over China's growing assertiveness in Asia.

item.title: BBC News: Burnham says he wants to cut welfare bill 'as soon as we possibly can'
item.description: Opponents have questioned the Budget's lack of detail on welfare reform, with the prime minister not outlining a timetable for any reductions.

item.title: The Guardian: Flávio Bolsonaro’s defeat is a major blow to Trump and his orange wave
item.description: The far-right candidate was supposed to claim the presidency, but Brazilian voters had other ideas For Donald Trump , Brazil’s presidential election was meant to represent the crest of the “orange wave” – a three-year su…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Israel’s anti-Qatar campaign bleeds into elections
item.description: Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesman rejects 'disinformation' amid allegations by some Israelis of voting interference.

item.title: Ars Technica: Massive leak exposes 41,000 DHS workers and undercover ICE agents
item.description: The leak reveals undercover agents, surveillance groups, and sensitive DHS access.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: I Gave My Blood to the AI Death Clock
item.description: Death Clock promises to predict when you’re going to die and help you extend your time on Earth. After a month, I felt like it was sucking the life out of me.

item.title: WIRED Science: An AI Breakthrough Has Made Decades of Computer Science Research ‘Irrelevant’
item.description: Anthropic and OpenAI say they’ve disproved a key tenet of computer science. Researchers are struggling with the fall but also feel like “overexcited bunnies” as they look at new questions to explore.

item.title: WIRED Business: The ‘Pain in the Ass’ Math That Could Save Vibe Coding From Itself
item.description: A new startup called &Truth is joining the race to automate formal verification, a painstaking process that uses math to prove software works as intended.

item.title: The New Yorker: How a Kansas Megachurch Pastor Might Determine Who Wins the Senate
item.description: Adam Hamilton’s campaign tests whether Democrats can find religion.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: Paris Hilton Defended Her Beauty and the Beast Costume
item.description: Her daughter didn’t even want to be dressed as Belle, okay?

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: The Latest Status Marker Is a 4-Bedroom Apartment
item.description: And new luxury condos are loaded with them.

item.description: Middle schoolers can meet teachers, tour classrooms and visit athletic facilities. The post Eastsiders can learn more about Warren Central at upcoming open house appeared first on Mirror Indy .
